records.description: Blend the existing RandomForest with a LightGBM classifier by equal-weight averaging of their test-set rank scores scaled to [0,1].

Replace the RandomForest and the old LightGBM in fit_predict with a single LGBMClassifier (400 trees, learning_rate 0.05, num_leaves 31, colsample 0.3, subsample 0.8 with subsample_freq 1, min_child_samples 10) and return its raw probabilities.

Append 11 RDKit physchem descriptors (MolWt, Crippen LogP, TPSA, H-bond donor and acceptor counts, rotatable bonds, aromatic and total ring counts, heavy atom count, Fsp3, formal-charge count) to each Morgan bit vector in featurize, so both the forest and LightGBM can split on them directly.
Append counts of acid, tetrazole, primary/secondary/tertiary aliphatic amine, quaternary ammonium, and sulfonamide SMARTS groups to each molecule's feature vector.

Replace the RF+LightGBM blend with a Tanimoto-kernel SVC: Morgan bit fingerprints only, a precomputed Jaccard kernel (sum-min over sum-max, computed via dot products), and SVC(C=1.0, probability=True, random_state=seed) returning class-1 probabilities.

Append the full rdkit.Chem.Descriptors.descList set (NaN/inf set to 0, each column clipped to the training-fold 1st-99th percentile range, with per-SMILES caching) to the Morgan bits and existing descriptors before the RF and LightGBM fits.

Append the full rdkit.Chem.Descriptors.descList set (NaN/inf set to 0, each column clipped to the training-fold 1st-99th percentile range, with per-SMILES caching) to the Morgan bits and existing descriptors before the RF and LightGBM fits.

issues: No integrity problems: the added AtomPair count fingerprint is computed from each molecule's SMILES alone, with no file access, pasted answers or use of test labels.
No bugs that invalidate the result: the count fingerprint is turned into float32 and joined to the existing features, and scale differences do not matter to a random forest.
Recomputed z = (0.0893 - 0.0949) / (0.0049 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/2)) ≈ -0.933, which matches the reported -0.929 within rounding. The candidate is worse but within noise, so reject is correct.

records.description: Adds a hashed 1024-bit atom-pair count fingerprint alongside the 2048-bit Morgan vector in featurize, so the RF and LightGBM models also see long-range topology.

Swap the standard Morgan atom invariants for the pharmacophoric feature-invariant generator (GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen, FCFP-style) while keeping radius 2 and 2048 bits, so substructure environments group donor, acceptor and aromatic atoms and may transfer better across unseen scaffolds.

Standardize each molecule before featurizing (keep the largest fragment, neutralize charges, drop stereochemistry) in both the fingerprint/descriptor path and the RDKit full-descriptor path, so salt forms and charge states of the same parent share one representation.

Replace the sklearn LGBMClassifier in the blend with a lgb.train booster (800 rounds, learning rate decaying linearly 0.1 to 0.01 via reset_parameter, feature_fraction 0.3, bagging 0.8) and use its probabilities in the rank average.

Replace the RandomForestClassifier with ExtraTreesClassifier (same n_estimators, max_features, min_samples_leaf, n_jobs and random_state) in the descriptor-plus-fingerprint tree ensemble, keeping the LightGBM blend unchanged.

Adds a Tanimoto k-nearest-neighbour score (k=10, similarity-cubed weighted mean of training labels, computed from the existing 2048-bit Morgan bits) as a third rank-averaged component alongside the RandomForest and LightGBM blend.

Add a CatBoostClassifier (500 iterations, depth 6, learning_rate 0.05, seeded) on the existing fingerprint plus descriptor matrix and include it as a third equal-weight member of the rank-averaged blend with the RandomForest and LightGBM models.

Replace the full-matrix LightGBM with four LightGBMs, one each on the Morgan bits, the 11 physchem columns, the full descList columns, and the fingerprint-free columns (physchem plus descList), each with colsample_bytree=0.5 and seed+g, then average rank-scaled predictions of these four plus the existing RF with equal weights.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff only switches the Morgan generator from binary bits (GetFingerprintAsNumPy) to counts (GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy). It adds no file or network access and does not touch the test labels.
No bug that would make the result meaningless. The count fingerprint keeps the same length (2048), and its integer values are merged with the float32 descriptors and cast to float32 without problems.

The z value checks out. Difference = 0.094 − 0.0893 = +0.0047 (a higher loss is worse). The standard deviation of the difference is 0.0049 × sqrt(1/1 + 1/2) ≈ 0.0060, so z ≈ −0.783. This matches the harness's −0.776 within rounding of the displayed means.
The rejection stands: the one candidate run scored worse than the incumbent mean, though the gap is within noise (|z| < 1).

records.description: Switch the Morgan features in featurize from 0/1 bit vectors to radius-2, 2048-bit count vectors via GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy, leaving the RandomForest and LightGBM settings unchanged.

Switch the LightGBM member from plain gbdt to DART boosting (drop_rate=0.1, skip_drop=0.5, max_drop=50) with n_estimators raised to 500 and learning_rate kept at 0.05, leaving the seeded rank-average blend with the RandomForest unchanged.

Regularize the LightGBM blend member with extra_trees, min_child_samples=40, reg_lambda=5.0, feature_fraction_bynode=0.2, bagging (0.7, freq 1), and 600 rounds at learning_rate 0.05, leaving the RandomForest and blend unchanged.

Adds four out-of-fold Ridge stacking features, each predicting MolWt, Crippen LogP, TPSA or HBD+HBA from the Morgan bits of the training fold (5-fold KFold seeded), and appends them to the RF and LightGBM inputs.

Before fitting the RF and LightGBM members, fit a quick 150-tree RandomForest on the training matrix only, keep the top 400 columns by impurity importance plus the 11 original physchem columns, and refit both members on that reduced matrix.
Append the 167-bit MACCS structural keys to each molecule's Morgan fingerprint and descriptor features inside featurize, so the RandomForest and LightGBM members both see them.

issues: No signs of gaming the measurement. There is no file or network access, no hard-coded answers, and no use of test labels. Featurization is done one molecule at a time and only from SMILES, so nothing leaks across folds.

The new code uses rdMolDescriptors._CalcCrippenContribs. The diff doesn't show the import block, so check that `from rdkit.Chem import rdMolDescriptors` is there. If it isn't, the job will crash with a NameError. That would cost a slot but would not make a score meaningless.
rdFingerprintGenerator, RADIUS and N_BITS are now unused. That's leftover clutter from the old Morgan path. Remove them or a linter may flag them again.
_CalcCrippenContribs is a private RDKit API. It works in current releases, but it could break if RDKit changes.

The WL hashing is deterministic: FNV over the repr of tuples of ints and bools, with neighbour labels sorted. Results don't depend on PYTHONHASHSEED, and features are the same across fits. Folding into 1024 bins causes some collisions, which is acceptable.
There are no run numbers yet, so z can't be computed and there are no claims to check.

records.description: Replace the 2048-bit Morgan bits with a 1024-bin hashed Weisfeiler-Lehman count vector (atom labels from element, degree, charge, aromaticity and 5-level binned Crippen contribution, refined over 3 neighbour-aggregation rounds), keeping the descriptor columns unchanged for the RF and LightGBM blend.

Appends four hand-built domain scores (a 5-part CNS MPO desirability sum, Lipinski violation count, Veber flag, and ionizable-group count) to the per-molecule descriptor block used by both RF and LightGBM.

issues: No measurement circumvention found: no file or network access, no pasted answers, no use of test labels. The meta-model is fit only on out-of-fold predictions derived from training data, and tanimoto_knn receives only train_y.

Design weakness (not a correctness bug): the inner StratifiedKFold is a random split, not scaffold-grouped, so near-duplicate molecules appear on both sides. The kNN feature therefore looks stronger in the out-of-fold matrix than under the harness's scaffold-disjoint scoring, likely over-weighting it in the logistic regression.

Train/apply mismatch typical of stacking: meta weights are learned from base models fit on 4/5 of the data but applied to base models fit on all of it (the kNN in particular sees more neighbours at predict time). Acceptable practice, but worth noting.
Complexity/cost: ~6 RF+LGBM fits plus kNN per harness fold (~90 fits per job) for no measured gain; this conflicts with the 'simpler is better' guidance.
Numbers are consistent with the harness: candidate 0.0900 vs incumbent 0.0893 is 0.0007 worse, well inside noise; recomputed z matches -0.116 and supports the provisional reject.

records.description: Stack the RandomForest, LightGBM and Tanimoto kNN base models through a LogisticRegression meta-model trained on their 5-fold inner out-of-fold probabilities, with test predictions from base models refit on the full training fold.

issues: No attempt to get around the measurement. The new code reads no files, uses no network and pastes in no answers. brics_counts uses only the molecule structure, never labels, and works the same way on train and test inputs.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. The fragment hash is a fixed sum of (i+1)*ord(c), not Python's hash(), so it gives the same result in every process and the features are the same in every fold.
Minor: the position-weighted character sum is a weak hash. Different BRICS fragments can collide in the 1024 bins, which may weaken the signal but does not make the result invalid.
Minor: the bare 'except Exception' silently returns an all-zero vector if decomposition fails. That is acceptable, but failures will not show up.

Minor: BRICSDecompose is called on every molecule each time featurize runs, which adds runtime. On 1624 small molecules it should stay far below the 10-minute limit, but the job time should be checked.
No GPU result exists yet, so there is no claim to check against numbers and z cannot be computed.

records.description: Append a 1024-bin stable-hash (zlib.crc32) count vector of BRICS fragment SMILES to each molecule's featurized row, leaving the models, descriptor clipping and seeding unchanged.

Swap the RandomForest member for an XGBClassifier (400 trees, depth 5, lr 0.05, subsample 0.8, colsample 0.3, min_child_weight 2, hist) in the rank-averaged blend with the existing LightGBM, leaving features and the LightGBM member unchanged.
Concatenate a hashed 1024-bin topological torsion count fingerprint (RDKit TopologicalTorsion generator) with the existing Morgan bits and descriptors in featurize.

Adds a third rank-averaged member: clipped descriptors are quantile-normalised and standardised on training data, mapped through 1000 seeded random Fourier features (RBF spectrum, gamma = 1/n_features), and fed to an L2 logistic regression with C = 0.1, weighted equally with the RF and LightGBM.

Adds a transductive Zhou label-spreading score over a top-10 symmetrised Tanimoto Morgan graph of train and test molecules (alpha 0.9, 30 iterations, training labels mapped to +1/-1), rank-blended into the existing RF+LightGBM ranks at weight 0.2.

Replace the sklearn LGBMClassifier member with a lgb.train booster whose init_score is the logit of a LogisticRegression on standardised MolWt, TPSA, HBD and charge count, adding that logit back to the raw score before the sigmoid at prediction time.

Pass LightGBM monotone_constraints (-1 for MolWt, TPSA, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors in both the 11-column block and the full descList block, found by name; 0 elsewhere, including Crippen LogP) so the boosted member is regularised by known BBB trends.

issues: Nothing in the diff gets around the measurement: no file or network access, no hard-coded answers, and no use of test labels. The QuantileTransformer is fit on training descriptors only and then applied to the test descriptors. The MLP is trained on y only, and its early stopping splits off part of the training fold.

`lo` and `hi` come from code outside the diff. Their names suggest clipping bounds taken from the training descriptors. If they were computed on the test set, that would only use unlabeled inputs, not labels, so it would not count as leakage.
No bug makes the result meaningless. The three-model rank average is correct, and all randomness uses the seed argument.

The numbers match the claim. The candidate's 0.094 is worse than the incumbent's 0.0893 by 0.0047. Using an sd of 0.0049 for the one candidate run and the two incumbent runs, the difference has an sd of 0.0049 × sqrt(1 + 1/2) ≈ 0.0060, so z ≈ -0.0047 / 0.0060 ≈ -0.78. Rejecting the candidate is correct.
Minor point: the MLP adds code and runtime for no gain, which also argues for rejecting it under the 'simpler is better' rule.

records.description: Adds a third rank-averaged member, an MLPClassifier (128,64 hidden units, alpha 1e-2, early stopping) trained on quantile-normalised clipped descriptors, blended with equal weight alongside the RandomForest and LightGBM.

Replace the single LightGBM member with 5 LightGBMs, each trained on a scaffold-level bootstrap (whole Murcko scaffold groups resampled with replacement via default_rng(seed+b)), and average their rank-scaled predictions as the gradient-boosting term in the blend.

Append eight single-conformer 3D shape descriptors (PMI1-3, NPR1-2, PBF, radius of gyration, asphericity; ETKDGv3 embedding with randomSeed=42, MMFF cleanup, zero fallback, per-SMILES cache) to the RDKit descriptor block, so the 1st-99th percentile clipping and both the RF and LightGBM members see them.

Add a third rank-averaged member, a LogisticRegression (C=0.5, max_iter=2000, seeded) fit on the 11 physchem descriptors standardized with a StandardScaler fitted on the training fold, and blend it equally with the existing RandomForest and LightGBM ranks.

Adds a third rank-averaged member: a logistic regression (C=0.1, no intercept) trained on 200k sampled positive-negative difference vectors of quantile-normalised full descriptors (fit on training data only), with equal weight alongside the RF and LightGBM ranks.

Add a third rank-averaged member, a logistic regression (C=0.1, max_iter=2000) on a spline-expanded, standardized clipped RDKit descriptor matrix (quantile-knot cubic B-spline basis, about 4 knots, fitted on the training fold), with the RF, LightGBM and spline-LR ranks blended at equal weight.

Adds a third rank-averaged member, a LogisticRegression (C=1.0, max_iter=2000) on character 2-5-gram TF-IDF of the raw SMILES (min_df=2, sublinear_tf, fitted on train only), and changes the blend to a three-way equal average of the RF, LightGBM and string-model ranks.
Add a third rank-averaged member, a linear ranker trained on about 200k sampled positive-negative difference vectors over quantile-scaled descriptors, to the RF+LightGBM blend.
Abort: the rotation-forest third member is not worth a slot, since every third rank-averaged member tried so far has been rejected.

Rank training molecules by the out-of-bag probability of their own label from a 100-tree RandomForest, then train the LightGBM member with lgb.train while ramping the weights of the hardest 40% from 0 to 1 over the first 150 of 300 rounds, leaving the RF member and rank blend unchanged.

Bag the RandomForest and LightGBM members over 5 scaffold-level bootstrap samples each (whole Murcko-scaffold groups resampled with replacement, seeded from the seed argument), and average the rank-scaled predictions across bags before the 50/50 blend.

memo: Helped: the RF+LightGBM blend (0.1194 vs baseline ~0.1361) and appending RDKit descriptors (11 physchem 0.1040; full descList 0.0944 and 0.0842, incumbent mean_adjusted 0.0893 over 2 runs). Descriptors drive the gain. Did not help: other fingerprint swaps or additions (atom-pair 0.0949, MACCS 0.0921, Morgan counts 0.0940, BRICS 0.0938), model swaps (XGBoost 0.1041, CatBoost 0.0950, ExtraTrees 0.0948, SVC 0.1255), LightGBM variants (DART 0.0967, regularized 0.0958, monotone 0.0942), and extra members like LR or MLP. Tanimoto kNN (0.0884), label spreading (0.0896), torsion counts (0.0902) and LR stacking (0.0900) were within noise. The two incumbent runs differ by about 0.01, twice the noise sd of ~0.0049, so single-run deltas under 0.01 are unreliable. Next: replicate the incumbent and the kNN variant to firm up the baseline. Tune blend weights and tree hyperparameters on the descriptors. Try fewer fingerprint bits. Avoid more fingerprint swaps, kernel models and model-family swaps.

incumbent.description: Append the full rdkit.Chem.Descriptors.descList set (NaN/inf set to 0, each column clipped to the training-fold 1st-99th percentile range, with per-SMILES caching) to the Morgan bits and existing descriptors before the RF and LightGBM fits.

backlog.spec: In featurize, replace GetFingerprintAsNumPy with GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy from the same radius-2 generator (keep 2048 bits), so each feature holds the number of times an environment occurs instead of a 0/1 bit. Leave the RandomForest settings unchanged. Count features often carry more signal than bits for property prediction.
backlog.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprints

backlog.spec: In featurize, compute a small set of interpretable descriptors per molecule (MolWt, MolLogP, TPSA, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, NumAromaticRings, RingCount, HeavyAtomCount, FractionCSP3, formal charge count) and concatenate them to the Morgan bit vector. Blood-brain barrier penetration is driven largely by TPSA, lipophilicity, and H-bond counts, so these give the forest direct access to them.
backlog.title: Add RDKit physchem descriptors to fingerprints

backlog.spec: Compute all values from rdkit.Chem.Descriptors.descList for each molecule, append them to the Morgan bits, replace NaN and infinite values with 0, and clip each column to its 1st-99th percentile range learned on the training fold. Use only training-fold statistics so no test information leaks in.
backlog.title: Full RDKit descriptor set with cleaning

backlog.spec: Compute the 167-bit MACCS structural keys with rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys for each molecule and concatenate them to the Morgan fingerprint before fitting the RandomForest. MACCS keys encode broad functional-group presence and are complementary to circular fingerprints.
backlog.title: Append MACCS keys

backlog.spec: Add a hashed atom-pair count fingerprint (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, 1024 bits, count mode) and concatenate it with the 2048-bit Morgan vector. Atom pairs capture long-range topology that radius-2 circular environments miss.
backlog.title: Atom-pair plus Morgan features

backlog.spec: Add a hashed topological torsion count fingerprint (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator, 1024 bits) and concatenate it with the Morgan features. Torsion paths describe local conformational and shape information that could help separate penetrating from non-penetrating molecules.
backlog.title: Topological torsion features

backlog.spec: Replace the standard Morgan generator with the feature-invariant variant (GetMorganGenerator with atomInvariantsGenerator set to rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen()), keeping radius 2 and 2048 bits. Pharmacophoric invariants group atoms by donor, acceptor, aromatic, and similar roles, which generalizes better across unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Feature-invariant Morgan (FCFP-style)

backlog.spec: In featurize, before computing fingerprints, keep only the largest covalent fragment (rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser), neutralize charges (rdMolStandardize.Uncharger), and remove stereochemistry with Chem.RemoveStereochemistry. This removes salt counter-ions and charge-state noise so that identical parent compounds share a representation.
backlog.title: Standardize molecules before featurizing

backlog.spec: Add a few counts computed by SMARTS patterns: carboxylic acids, tetrazoles, primary/secondary/tertiary aliphatic amines, quaternary ammonium, and sulfonamides. Concatenate these counts to the fingerprint. Acidic groups are known to reduce BBB penetration and basic amines often increase it, so ionization-related features are informative.
backlog.title: Ionization-class and acid/base group counts

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestClassifier with ExtraTreesClassifier using the same n_estimators, max_features, min_samples_leaf, n_jobs=-1, and random_state=seed. Extremely randomized splits give smoother probability estimates and often generalize better on small, noisy datasets like this one.
backlog.title: Switch RandomForest to ExtraTrees

backlog.spec: Replace the RandomForest with an LGBMClassifier (about 400 trees, learning_rate 0.05, num_leaves 31, feature_fraction 0.3, bagging_fraction 0.8 with bagging_freq 1, min_child_samples 10, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8). Gradient boosting often outperforms bagged trees on sparse binary fingerprint features.
backlog.title: LightGBM classifier on fingerprints

backlog.spec: Replace the RandomForest with an XGBClassifier (about 400 estimators, max_depth 5, learning_rate 0.05, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.3, min_child_weight 2, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8, tree_method hist). Use it to fit the training fold and return predict_proba[:,1] for the test molecules.
backlog.title: XGBoost classifier on fingerprints

backlog.spec: Use CatBoostClassifier with about 500 iterations, depth 6, learning_rate 0.05, random_seed=seed, verbose=False, thread_count=8, on the concatenated fingerprint and physchem descriptor matrix. CatBoost's ordered boosting is robust to overfitting on small datasets with many binary features.
backlog.title: CatBoost classifier on fingerprints and descriptors

backlog.spec: Compute Morgan bit-vector fingerprints, build a precomputed Tanimoto (Jaccard) similarity kernel K(a,b)=sum(min)/sum(max) for train-train and test-train pairs, and fit sklearn SVC(kernel='precomputed', C=1.0, probability=True, random_state=seed). Return predict_proba[:,1]. Tanimoto kernels are the standard chemically meaningful similarity measure for fingerprints.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-kernel SVM

backlog.spec: Compute the Tanimoto similarity matrix between test and training Morgan fingerprints. For each test molecule take the k=10 most similar training molecules and return the similarity-weighted mean of their labels (weights = similarity to the power 3). This nearest-neighbour score is a cheap, different model to blend with the forest.
backlog.title: Tanimoto k-nearest-neighbour vote

backlog.spec: Build a feature matrix of physchem descriptors (MolWt, MolLogP, TPSA, HBD, HBA, rotatable bonds, aromatic rings, charge counts), standardize it with StandardScaler fitted on the training fold, and fit LogisticRegression(C=0.5, max_iter=2000, random_state=seed). Return its predicted probabilities. Its near-linear structure is a useful low-variance baseline to blend with the forest.
backlog.title: Logistic regression on scaled descriptors

backlog.spec: Train the existing RandomForest and a LGBMClassifier (learning_rate 0.05, 300 trees, num_leaves 15, feature_fraction 0.3, random_state=seed) on the same features. Convert each model's test-set probabilities to ranks scaled to [0,1] and return their equal-weight average. Averaging ranks keeps the output on a probability-like scale and combines two model families.
backlog.title: Rank-average blend of RF and gradient boosting

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, split the training fold into 5 stratified inner folds. Generate out-of-fold probabilities for the RandomForest, a LightGBM classifier, and the Tanimoto kNN score; then fit a LogisticRegression meta-model on these three columns. For test molecules, average the base models trained on the full training fold and pass them through the meta-model.
backlog.title: Stacked ensemble with logistic meta-model

backlog.spec: Use sklearn MLPClassifier with hidden_layer_sizes=(256,), activation relu, alpha=1e-3 (L2 weight decay), learning_rate_init=1e-3, batch_size=64, max_iter=200, early_stopping=True with validation_fraction=0.1, random_state=seed on the Morgan bit vector. Return predict_proba[:,1]. A small regularized neural net offers a different inductive bias from trees.
backlog.title: MLP on fingerprints with weight decay

backlog.spec: Train three RandomForestClassifier models with n_estimators=300 each and random_state values seed, seed+1000, seed+2000, then average their predict_proba outputs. Averaging independently seeded forests reduces variance beyond what a single larger forest gives, and it stays within the seed argument rule.
backlog.title: Average several RF seeds in fit_predict

backlog.spec: Set RandomForestClassifier max_samples=0.6 with bootstrap=True and increase n_estimators to 600. Smaller bootstrap samples decorrelate trees more strongly, which often improves ranking quality (AUROC) on noisy, small datasets while keeping the forest size reasonable.
backlog.title: Subsample rows per tree (smaller bootstrap)

backlog.spec: Set class_weight='balanced_subsample' in RandomForestClassifier. If the positive class is the majority or minority in this dataset, weighting shifts the leaf probabilities and can improve the ranking that AUROC measures, without changing the features or tree count.
backlog.title: Balanced class weights in the forest

backlog.spec: Set MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF to 3 in the RandomForest. Pure leaves in a forest of single-sample leaves give probabilities that are 0 or 1 too often, producing ties and a coarse ranking. Requiring at least 3 samples per leaf gives finer-grained scores and reduces overfitting to noisy labels.
backlog.title: Larger minimum leaf size for smoother probabilities

backlog.spec: Set max_depth=12 in RandomForestClassifier, keeping the other settings. Limiting depth controls memorization of individual molecules and scaffolds, which should help generalization across unseen Murcko scaffolds in this grouped evaluation.
backlog.title: Cap tree depth in the forest

backlog.spec: Before fitting, drop columns of the training fingerprint matrix whose frequency across training molecules is below 1% or above 99% (computed on training fold only), and apply the same column mask to the test matrix. Removing rare and near-universal bits reduces noise and speeds up the forest's split search.
backlog.title: Remove near-constant fingerprint bits

backlog.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold of each training molecule (MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles). Give each molecule a training weight inversely proportional to the number of training molecules sharing its scaffold, normalized to mean 1, and pass these as sample_weight to the RandomForest fit. This stops heavily represented scaffold families from dominating the trees.
backlog.title: Sample weights by scaffold frequency

backlog.spec: Fit the RandomForest once, predict the test molecules, and add the test molecules whose predicted probability is above 0.9 or below 0.1 to the training set with their predicted hard labels. Refit the forest on the augmented set and return its probabilities for the test molecules. This transductive step adapts the model to the unseen scaffolds in the test fold.
backlog.title: Self-training with confident test pseudo-labels

backlog.spec: Train an LGBMClassifier with 800 boosting rounds, using learning_rate as a callable schedule passed through the reset_parameter callback that decays linearly from 0.1 to 0.01 over the rounds (use lgb.train with a dataset and then wrap predictions), feature_fraction 0.3, bagging_fraction 0.8, and random seed. The decaying step size usually improves generalization over a fixed rate.
backlog.title: LightGBM with decaying learning rate schedule

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, hold out a stratified 15% of the training fold for validation. Train an LGBMClassifier with up to 1000 rounds (learning_rate 0.03, feature_fraction 0.3, bagging_fraction 0.8) and early_stopping_rounds=50 on the validation split, then refit on the full training fold using the best iteration count (scaled by 1.1). Automatic round selection avoids a hand-picked and possibly overfit tree count.
backlog.title: Early-stopped boosting with inner validation

backlog.spec: Keep the existing full-descriptor and fingerprint features. Add a third LightGBM model trained with objective='rank_xendcg' (or 'lambdarank') on a single query group containing all training rows, with the same n_estimators=300, learning_rate=0.05, num_leaves=15 and colsample_bytree=0.3. Its scores are only ordered, so convert them to ranks with scaled_rank and add them to the existing rank-average blend with equal weight. Seed it through random_state=seed. Rationale: the metric is AUROC, so a pairwise or listwise ranking loss should target it more directly than logloss.
backlog.title: LightGBM ranking objective to optimise AUROC directly

backlog.spec: Replace the gradient-boosted member's plain gbdt with boosting_type='dart' (drop_rate=0.1, skip_drop=0.5, max_drop=50), keep the rest, and raise n_estimators to 500 with learning_rate=0.05 since DART drops trees during training. DART randomly drops earlier trees each iteration, which regularises the ensemble and often helps on small noisy tabular data. Keep the seed in random_state. The blend stays rank-average of RF and this model.
backlog.title: DART boosting for the LightGBM member

backlog.spec: In the LightGBM member, pass monotone_constraints so that the physchem columns with known direction are constrained: MolWt, TPSA, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors and the count of Lipinski-type polar atoms are -1 (more polar or bulky means less likely to cross the BBB); Crippen LogP is +1 only up to a cap, so leave it at 0 if unsure. All other columns are 0. Identify column indices by name from the Descriptors.descList order and the 11-column block. This injects prior chemistry as a regulariser, reducing spurious splits on small-sample noise.
backlog.title: Monotone constraints on known physicochemical trends

backlog.spec: Add a fundamentally different view that ignores RDKit featurisation: build a character n-gram TF-IDF matrix from the raw SMILES strings (analyzer='char', ngram_range=(2,5), min_df=2, sublinear_tf=True) fitted on train_smiles only, then fit a LogisticRegression(C=1.0, max_iter=2000, class_weight=None, random_state=seed). Score test_smiles with predict_proba and add its scaled_rank to the existing blend with weight 1/3, replacing the equal-weight 0.5/0.5 average with a three-way equal average. The string model captures syntax-level motifs that Morgan bits may miss.
backlog.title: Character n-gram TF-IDF on SMILES with logistic regression

backlog.spec: Instead of one LightGBM fit, train 5 LightGBM models, each on a bootstrap that resamples whole Murcko scaffold groups from train_smiles (compute scaffolds with MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles on each training molecule; sample scaffold IDs with replacement using a np.random.default_rng(seed + b) for bag b; take all rows of each drawn scaffold). Each bag uses the same parameters as the existing LightGBM, with random_state=seed+b. Average the bags' rank-scaled predictions and use that as the gradient-boosting term in the blend. This makes each bag see a different skeleton mix, which matches the scaffold-split evaluation.
backlog.title: Scaffold-bootstrap bagging of LightGBM

backlog.spec: Change the fingerprint part of featurize to radius 1 with 512 bits (the N_BITS and RADIUS settings) while keeping the full descList block exactly as now. Rationale: the notes show descriptors drive the gain, and a 2048-bit fingerprint dilutes feature sampling for the RF (max_features=0.3) and LightGBM (colsample_bytree=0.3). Keep the blend unchanged. Only the fingerprint width and radius change, so a single run should show whether the bit block is hurting the descriptor signal.
backlog.title: Descriptor-dominant features with a smaller Morgan radius-1 block

backlog.spec: Add a third model: take the full descriptor matrix D_train and D_test (already cleaned and clipped), fit sklearn.preprocessing.QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal', n_quantiles=200) on train only, then train sklearn.neural_network.MLPClassifier(hidden_layer_sizes=(128,64), alpha=1e-2, early_stopping=True, validation_fraction=0.15, max_iter=500, random_state=seed). Rank-scale its test probabilities and add them to the blend with equal weight. The quantile transform removes the heavy tails of descriptors such as MolWt and BertzCT, which otherwise disturb neural nets.
backlog.title: Quantile-transformed descriptors into a small MLP

backlog.spec: Add a probabilistic non-tree model: quantile-transform the full cleaned descriptor matrix (as above), then reduce to the top 64 columns by mutual_info_classif on the training set (random_state=seed), and fit sklearn.gaussian_process.GaussianProcessClassifier with kernel ConstantKernel()*RBF(length_scale=np.ones(64)*5.0) and n_restarts_optimizer=0. Score test rows with predict_proba and rank-average the result into the blend at weight 1/3. The GP gives smooth, similarity-based probabilities in descriptor space that differ from tree splits and can help AUROC on the unseen-skeleton folds.
backlog.title: Gaussian-process classifier on quantile-scaled descriptors

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, run a 5-fold inner stratified split on train_smiles (seeded by seed) with the existing RF plus LightGBM blend, record out-of-fold scores, and drop training rows whose out-of-fold rank score is on the wrong side of the label by a large margin (for example, label 1 with score below the 10th percentile, or label 0 with score above the 90th percentile). Refit the full blend on the cleaned set and predict test_smiles. The inner split must use scaffold grouping so the cleaning mirrors the evaluation. This is a noise-removal step for label errors in the BBB data, and it does not change the features.
backlog.title: Remove confidently mislabelled training molecules before fitting

backlog.spec: Split the feature matrix into 4 column groups: the 2048-bit Morgan block, the 11 physchem descriptors, the remaining full descList columns, and the fingerprint-free set. Train one LightGBM per group, each with random_state=seed+g and colsample_bytree=0.5, and also one RF on the full matrix as now. Average the rank-scaled predictions of the four group models plus the RF with equal weights. This gives diverse views that each model can exploit independently and reduces the chance that one dominant block masks the others.
backlog.title: Feature-subspace ensemble across descriptor families

backlog.spec: Add a separate model in fit_predict: take the clipped full RDKit descriptor matrix (D_train, D_test), standardize it with statistics from the training fold, and expand each column with a natural cubic spline basis (about 4 knots at training quantiles). Fit sklearn LogisticRegression (L2, C around 0.1, max_iter 2000) on the expanded matrix. Convert its test probabilities to scaled ranks and blend them with the existing RF and LightGBM ranks at equal weight. The aim is to capture the non-monotone, saturating effects of TPSA, MW and logP on BBB penetration, which trees approximate only coarsely.
backlog.title: Spline-expanded descriptor logistic regression

backlog.spec: Replace the current LGBMClassifier member with a LightGBM model that has linear_tree=True (piecewise-linear leaf models, linear_lambda=1.0), trained on the same matrix of Morgan bits plus clipped descriptors. Keep num_leaves at 15 and colsample_bytree at 0.3, and use min_child_samples=20 so the linear fits are stable. Keep the RF and the rank blend unchanged. This gives the boosting member smooth within-leaf trends in the physicochemical columns, without adding new features.
backlog.title: LightGBM with linear leaves on descriptors

backlog.spec: Change only the LightGBM member's regularization: extra_trees=True, min_child_samples=40, reg_lambda=5.0, feature_fraction_bynode=0.2, and bagging_fraction=0.7 with bagging_freq=1. Raise n_estimators to 600 and keep learning_rate at 0.05. Pass the seed into the constructor. The randomized split thresholds and strong leaf constraints should reduce overfitting to scaffold-specific bits, which is the main failure mode when test skeletons are unseen.
backlog.title: Extremely randomized, heavily regularized LightGBM

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, first fit a quick RandomForest (150 trees, max_features 0.3) on the full training matrix. Keep the top 400 columns by impurity importance (always keeping the 11 original physchem columns), then refit the existing RF and LightGBM members on this reduced matrix only. Derive the selection from training data only, so no test information leaks in. The goal is to drop the many near-useless Morgan and descriptor columns that dilute the feature sampling of both the forest and the boosting model.
backlog.title: Importance-based feature pruning inside each fold

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, pick 4 continuous targets that are available from RDKit: MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt and NumHDonors+NumHAcceptors. For each, fit a Ridge regressor on the Morgan bit matrix of the training fold, and produce out-of-fold predictions for the training rows using a 5-fold KFold split with the seed. Predict the test rows from a model fit on all training rows. Append these 4 predicted values as extra columns to X_train and X_test before fitting RF and LightGBM. This is a learned, supervised compression of the fingerprint into physically meaningful axes, not a raw descriptor.
backlog.title: Out-of-fold physchem regression stacking features

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, train a logistic-regression domain classifier that separates the training rows (label 0) from the test rows (label 1), using standardized clipped descriptors plus Morgan bits. Compute w = p/(1-p) for each training row, clip w to the range [0.2, 5] and normalize its mean to 1. Pass w as sample_weight to the RF and LightGBM fits. The test molecules are only seen through their features, so this is a transductive reweighting. It shifts capacity toward training molecules that look like the unseen test skeletons. Use the seed for the domain classifier.
backlog.title: Density-ratio importance weighting toward the test distribution

backlog.spec: Append a short block of domain composite scores to the feature matrix. Compute the CNS multiparameter optimization score from the RDKit values of ClogP, MolWt, TPSA, HBD, and the count of basic amine and acid groups as a rough pKa proxy, each mapped through the published monotone desirability functions and summed to a 0–6 score. Also add Lipinski violation count, Veber violation flag, and the number of ionizable groups. Append these 4 to the features used by RF and LightGBM. These are compact, hand-designed priors that tree models cannot easily build from raw columns.
backlog.title: CNS MPO and rule-based composite features

backlog.spec: Replace the Morgan featurizer's atom invariant with a WL-style iterative refinement. Start from a per-atom label built from element, degree, formal charge, aromaticity, and Crippen contribution binned to 5 levels. Run 3 rounds: at each round, each atom's new label is a hash of its own label and the sorted labels of its neighbours. Count all labels across the 3 rounds and hash them into 1024 bins, which yields a counts vector. Use this count vector in place of the Morgan bits for the RF and LightGBM. The idea is a longer-range, property-weighted substructure code that keeps the descriptor columns unchanged.
backlog.title: Weisfeiler-Lehman neighbourhood aggregation of atom properties

backlog.spec: Train one LightGBM model with n_estimators=600 and learning_rate 0.05, but instead of keeping only the final model, take predictions at iterations 150, 300, 450 and 600 by calling predict_proba with num_iteration set to each value on the fitted model. Convert each snapshot's test predictions to scaled ranks and average them, and use this averaged rank as the LightGBM component in the blend. This adds a cheap, seed-consistent averaging over boosting trajectories, with no extra fitting cost.
backlog.title: Snapshot ensemble of LightGBM checkpoints

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, fit sklearn TruncatedSVD (n_components=64, random_state=seed) on the Morgan bit matrix of the training fold only, then transform both train and test fingerprints. Append the 64 SVD scores to the existing feature matrix (fingerprint bits, clipped descriptors) for the RF and LightGBM members. Because the SVD sees only training rows and is unsupervised, there is no label leakage. The dense low-rank summaries give each tree a set of broadly informative axes where single bits are sparse.
backlog.title: Truncated SVD of the fingerprint as dense appended features

backlog.spec: In featurize, add a fragment-based block alongside the Morgan bits. For each molecule, run rdkit.Chem.BRICS.BRICSDecompose(mol) to get the set of BRICS fragment SMILES, hash each fragment string into a 1024-bin count vector with a stable hash (e.g. zlib.crc32 modulo 1024, not Python's salted hash), and append these counts to X. Keep everything else unchanged, including the descriptor clipping. Use the seed only for the existing models. Molecules that BRICS cannot fragment give an all-zero block, which is fine.
backlog.title: BRICS fragment count fingerprint

backlog.spec: For each molecule, embed one conformer with rdkit.Chem.AllChem.EmbedMolecule using ETKDG and a fixed random seed (randomSeed=42), with a fallback to 0 features if embedding fails. Optionally run a quick MMFF optimisation with a capped iteration count. From the conformer compute the principal moments of inertia (CalcPMI1/2/3), normalised PMI ratios (NPR1, NPR2), PBF, radius of gyration, asphericity, and CalcWHIM or CalcRDF if they are fast. Clip these to the 1st-99th percentile of the training set, as the descriptors already are, and append them to the feature matrix for both the RF and the LightGBM member. Cache results per SMILES in a dict to keep the cost down.
backlog.title: Single-conformer 3D shape descriptors

backlog.spec: Replace the RF+LightGBM blend with a from-scratch graph neural network written in numpy. Atom features: element one-hot for the common elements, degree, total H count, formal charge, aromaticity, and in-ring flag. Use 3 rounds of message passing: each atom sums its neighbours' hidden vectors, then applies a shared dense layer with ReLU and a residual connection. Use hidden size 64. Global sum pooling and mean pooling are concatenated with the standardised, clipped RDKit descriptors, then a dense sigmoid output. Train with full-batch or minibatch Adam, learning rate 1e-3, weight decay 1e-4, about 150 epochs, with the seed controlling initialisation. Average 3 seeds and rank-blend the output 50/50 with the existing LightGBM member. Keep the total fit time per fold under 30 seconds.
backlog.title: Small numpy message-passing graph network

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, before the final fit, run a small grid search for the LightGBM member using an inner GroupKFold split on the training molecules, with groups given by the Murcko scaffold SMILES. The grid has about 6 settings varying num_leaves in {7, 15, 31}, min_child_samples in {10, 30}, and colsample_bytree in {0.2, 0.4}. For each setting, compute the inner-fold mean AUROC with sklearn's roc_auc_score. Refit LightGBM on all training data with the best setting and use it in the blend. Keep the RF unchanged. Use the seed for every inner split and model so the result is reproducible, and make sure the total time per fit_predict call stays well under the 10-minute budget.
backlog.title: Inner scaffold-CV hyperparameter selection for LightGBM

backlog.spec: Before fitting any model, denoise the training labels. Compute the Tanimoto similarity matrix of Morgan bit vectors among the training molecules only. For each training molecule, take its k=5 most similar other training molecules and set a soft label y_s = 0.7 * y_i + 0.3 * (mean of their labels weighted by similarity). Threshold the result at 0.5 to get hard labels, or keep the soft values by fitting the RF on the 0/1 labels with sample_weight equal to 1 and LightGBM on the soft targets via a regression objective on the same features. Choose the variant by the inner-fold AUROC. The test predictions and everything else stay the same.
backlog.title: kNN label denoising of training targets

backlog.spec: Add a graph-based scorer alongside the RF and LightGBM. Build a Tanimoto similarity matrix over the union of training and test molecules using Morgan bit vectors, keep only the top 10 neighbours per node (symmetrised), and form the normalised graph matrix S = D^-1/2 W D^-1/2. Iterate Zhou-style label spreading F <- alpha * S F + (1 - alpha) * Y0 with alpha = 0.9 for about 30 iterations. Here Y0 holds the training labels (mapped to +1/-1 or 0/1) and zeros for test nodes. Read the spreading scores for the test rows, rank-scale them, and blend them with the existing tree ranks at a weight of 0.2 for the graph score. This is transductive but uses only the training labels and the test SMILES, which the harness provides.
backlog.title: Transductive label propagation over train and test

backlog.spec: Train a first pass of the existing RF and LightGBM using the normal training data. Compute out-of-fold predictions on the training molecules with a 5-fold GroupKFold grouped by scaffold, using the seed. Identify training molecules whose out-of-fold rank is on the wrong side of the label, for example positives with a low score or negatives with a high score, and set their sample weight to 2.0 while leaving the rest at 1.0. Refit both models with these sample weights and blend the new predictions with the same rank-average. This targets the hard, possibly noisy molecules without removing them.
backlog.title: Two-pass hard-example reweighting

backlog.spec: Split the training molecules into 3 bins by heavy-atom count using the 33rd and 67th percentiles of the training set. Train one LightGBM per bin with the same feature matrix (Morgan bits plus clipped descriptors), plus one global LightGBM on all data. For each test molecule, assign it to its size bin and blend the expert score with the global score by an equal-weight rank average. If a bin has fewer than 80 training molecules, fall back to the global model for that bin. Keep the RF in the blend as is, so the final output is the rank average of the RF, the global LightGBM, and the bin expert.
backlog.title: Molecular-size mixture of experts

backlog.spec: Train two separate models on the training data: a fingerprint-only model (LightGBM on the 2048 Morgan bits) and a descriptor-only model (RF on the clipped full descriptor list). For each round, use each model to score the test molecules and take the 10% most confident test predictions from each (highest and lowest rank) as pseudo-labels for the other view. Add those pseudo-labelled test rows to the other view's training set and refit. Run 2 rounds, then return the rank average of the final two models' test predictions. The procedure is transductive and uses only the test SMILES, not the test labels.
backlog.title: Two-view co-training with fingerprint and descriptor models

backlog.spec: Add a kernel-approximation model that is cheap and different from the trees. Take the quantile-transformed (rank-based to a normal distribution) clipped descriptors, standardise them using training-set statistics, and map them with 1000 random Fourier features, cos(X W + b) with W drawn from a Gaussian of scale gamma = 1/n_features and b uniform on [0, 2pi], both seeded. Fit an L2-regularised logistic regression on these features with C = 0.1 (sklearn LogisticRegression, lbfgs). Return its scaled rank as a third member of the rank-average blend with the RF and LightGBM, at equal weight. Do not change the fingerprint features.
backlog.title: Random Fourier features with a linear classifier on descriptors

backlog.spec: Keep the existing LGBMClassifier member but train it on softened targets: replace each 0/1 label with 0.05 or 0.95 (eps=0.05). Use LightGBM's lgb.train with objective='cross_entropy', which accepts probabilities as labels, with the same num_leaves=15, colsample_bytree=0.3, learning_rate=0.05, 300 rounds and seed. Predict with the booster and keep the rank-average blend unchanged. Smoothing discourages overconfident leaves on noisy BBB labels and may improve AUROC across unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Label-smoothed cross-entropy LightGBM

backlog.spec: Add a linear model trained directly on the AUROC objective. Quantile-scale the full descriptor matrix (clip to train 1st/99th percentiles, then map to ranks or z-scores on train). Sample about 200k random positive-negative pairs from the training set, form difference vectors x_pos - x_neg with label 1 and x_neg - x_pos with label 0, and fit sklearn LogisticRegression(C=0.1, fit_intercept=False) on them. Score test molecules by w.x, convert to a rank in [0,1], and add it as a third member of the existing rank-average blend with weight 1/3 each. This optimises pairwise ordering, the quantity the metric measures, instead of pointwise log-loss.
backlog.title: Pairwise AUROC-optimising linear ranker

backlog.spec: Before fitting the LightGBM member, make 3 noisy copies of the training matrix. Each copy adds N(0, 0.05 * IQR_j) noise to every descriptor column j (IQR computed on the training data, fingerprint bits left unchanged), using a numpy RandomState seeded from the seed argument. Stack the original and the copies (4x rows) with labels repeated, and fit LGBMClassifier with the same hyperparameters but min_child_samples raised to 40 to offset the duplicated rows. The augmentation smooths split thresholds over the descriptor space and should help generalisation to new scaffolds.
backlog.title: Gaussian-jitter augmentation of descriptors

backlog.spec: After computing the blended test scores, smooth them transductively. Standardise the test descriptor matrix with the training mean and sd, find each test molecule's k=5 nearest test neighbours (Euclidean, sklearn NearestNeighbors fit on test only), and replace the score with 0.5*own score + 0.5*mean of neighbour scores. Use rank-scaled scores before and after. Molecules with similar physicochemical profiles in the same batch tend to share BBB status, so this denoises individual predictions at no training cost.
backlog.title: Test-neighbourhood smoothing of predictions

backlog.spec: Address covariate shift between training and test scaffolds. Currently the clipping bounds come from the training set only. Instead, map each descriptor column of the test matrix through the empirical CDF of the test set itself (rank within test, scaled to [0,1]) and map the training matrix through its own CDF, so both are on comparable quantile scales before tree fitting; for the trees, keep the raw clipped values for training and use the quantile-mapped values only to decide the final probability via a 50/50 average of predictions from the raw-feature and quantile-feature models. Applied consistently across all 15 folds, this tests whether a distribution-matched view of the descriptors helps.
backlog.title: Per-split quantile normalisation of test descriptors

backlog.spec: Add a diverse, very cheap member. Binarise each descriptor column into 8 quantile bins using training-set edges, one-hot encode the bins, and concatenate with the 2048 Morgan bits. Fit sklearn BernoulliNB(alpha=1.0) on this binary matrix. Blend its test-set rank score into the existing rank average with weight 0.2, renormalising the other two weights to 0.4 each. Naive Bayes makes strongly different errors from trees and is nearly free to fit, so it may add ensemble diversity.
backlog.title: Naive Bayes member on binarised descriptors and fingerprint bits

backlog.spec: Learn a compact dense representation with a small denoising autoencoder implemented in plain numpy. Input: the concatenated standardised Morgan bits and quantile-scaled descriptors from the training set. Architecture: one hidden layer of 128 tanh units with a 32-unit bottleneck and a linear decoder. Train with Adam (lr 1e-3), weight decay 1e-4, input dropout 0.2 (noise corruption), batch size 128, for 60 epochs, seeded from the seed argument. Append the 32 bottleneck activations of train and test molecules to the feature matrix for the existing RF and LightGBM members. Train the autoencoder on training molecules only, so no test information leaks.
backlog.title: Denoising autoencoder bottleneck features in numpy

backlog.spec: Start LightGBM from a simple BBB rule rather than from zero log-odds. Fit a small sklearn LogisticRegression(C=1.0) on the four standardised features TPSA, MolWt, number of H-bond donors and formal-charge count (training set only). Compute its logit for train and test molecules and pass it to LightGBM as init_score for the training data in lgb.train, using the raw margin of the rule as the starting point. At prediction time add the same logit to the booster's raw score before applying the sigmoid. This makes the trees model the residual from a physically motivated baseline, so they spend capacity on the hard cases.
backlog.title: Physicochemical prior as boosting init_score

backlog.spec: Vary the column sampling over the course of boosting. Train LightGBM in four stages of 75 rounds each, using lgb.train with init_model/keep_training_booster so each stage continues the previous booster. Set feature_fraction to 0.1 in stage 1, 0.2 in stage 2, 0.35 in stage 3 and 0.5 in stage 4, with learning_rate 0.05 throughout and num_leaves=15. Early rounds then pick broad, noisy splits and later rounds focus on the strongest descriptors. Compare against the current constant colsample_bytree=0.3 with the same total of 300 rounds.
backlog.title: Feature-fraction schedule across boosting rounds

backlog.spec: Reduce variance from random seeds with a batch of bootstrap models. In fit_predict, form 5 bootstrap samples of the training data drawn at the scaffold level (group rows by Murcko scaffold, draw scaffolds with replacement, take all their molecules). For each bootstrap, fit the current RandomForest with 100 trees and the LightGBM member, keep the rank-scaled test predictions, and average them across bootstraps before the final blend. Keep total time under the job limit by reducing per-model trees to fit the 10-minute budget. Scaffold bootstraps match the grouped evaluation and may stabilise the decision function across unseen skeletons.
backlog.title: Scaffold-level seed averaging with bootstrapped scaffolds

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, group training molecules by Murcko scaffold. Train 5 LightGBM models (same settings as the current gb) plus 5 RF models, each on a bootstrap sample drawn at the scaffold-group level (resample scaffolds with replacement, keep all molecules of each drawn scaffold), with seeds derived from the seed argument. Average the rank-scaled predictions across the bags. This decorrelates members in a way the random row bootstrap does not, and is meant to help generalisation to unseen skeletons.
backlog.title: Scaffold-level seed averaging via bootstrapped scaffold groups

backlog.spec: Replace one blend member with a linear model trained directly on AUROC. Quantile-transform the full descriptor matrix (fit on training data only), then sample up to 200k random positive-negative pairs from the training set, and fit a logistic regression on the difference vectors x_pos minus x_neg with label 1 (and the negated differences with label 0), using L2 regularisation with C=0.1. Score test molecules with the linear function. Rank-average this score with the existing RF and LightGBM ranks at equal weight.
backlog.title: Pairwise AUROC-optimising linear ranker on descriptors

backlog.spec: Train two separate models: one RF on the 2048 Morgan bits only, and one LightGBM on the 11 physchem columns plus the clipped full descriptor list. Each model is then used to pseudo-label the test set: take the test molecules where one view is most confident (top and bottom 10 percent of its rank), add those as pseudo-labelled rows to the other view's training set, and refit. Final output is the rank-average of the two refitted views. The fingerprint and descriptor views are assumed to be conditionally independent given the label, which is the premise of co-training.
backlog.title: Two-view co-training between fingerprint and descriptor models

backlog.spec: Train a logistic classifier that separates training molecules from test molecules using the descriptor matrix (standardised, fit on train plus test). Convert its predicted odds into importance weights for training samples, clip the weights to [0.2, 5], and normalise to mean 1. Pass these weights as sample_weight to both the RF and LightGBM fits. The intent is to emphasise training molecules that look like the unseen test skeletons, which is the target of the benchmark.
backlog.title: Density-ratio importance weighting toward the test distribution

backlog.spec: Split training molecules into three heavy-atom-count bins by tertiles (fit thresholds on the training set). Fit a separate LightGBM and a separate RF on each bin. For each test molecule, predict with the expert of its bin, and additionally average in the global model with weight 0.3. Output rank-scaled probabilities. Smaller molecules and larger molecules follow different penetration rules, so local experts may capture differences that a single global tree split misses.
backlog.title: Molecular-size mixture of experts

backlog.spec: After the blended rank score is computed for the test molecules, build the Tanimoto similarity matrix among test molecules only (Morgan bit fingerprints). For each test molecule keep its 5 nearest test neighbours with similarity above 0.3, and replace its score with 0.7 times its own score plus 0.3 times the mean score of those neighbours. If no neighbour passes the threshold, keep the original score. Re-rank the result with scaled_rank. This exploits local structure within the held-out fold, which is a different use of test data from the previously tried label spreading.
backlog.title: Test-neighbourhood smoothing of predictions

backlog.spec: Before fitting the final models, run a 5-fold cross-validated RF on the training set using the same features. Mark as suspicious any training molecule whose out-of-fold predicted probability for its own label is below 0.1. Drop those rows (at most 10 percent of training data, keep the 10 percent with lowest own-label probability at most) and fit the RF and LightGBM blend on the remaining rows. The benchmark's BBB labels are noisy, so removing confidently contradicted examples may sharpen the decision boundary on unseen skeletons.
backlog.title: Label-noise filtering before fitting

backlog.spec: Augment the training descriptor matrix for the LightGBM member only. Make 3 noisy copies of each training row, adding independent Gaussian noise to each standardised descriptor column with standard deviation 0.05 (after quantile scaling fitted on training data). Concatenate the copies with the original labels and fit LightGBM with the same hyperparameters. The RF stays on the unaugmented features. Smoothing the decision function in descriptor space is a regulariser aimed at the cross-scaffold generalisation gap.
backlog.title: Gaussian-jitter augmentation of descriptor rows

backlog.spec: Replace the single LightGBM fit with one training run of 600 boosting rounds using a cosine-annealed learning rate from 0.1 down to 0.005, via the lgb.train callback mechanism (learning_rate_schedule through reset_parameter). Save predictions on the test set at rounds 200, 400 and 600 and average their rank-scaled outputs as the LightGBM member. The snapshot average is a cheap ensemble from a single run and uses a schedule different from the constant-rate and decaying-rate attempts already tried.
backlog.title: Snapshot LightGBM with a cosine learning-rate schedule

backlog.spec: Keep the existing LightGBM member but replace its binary logloss with a focal loss (gamma=2, alpha=0.5) passed as a custom objective to lgb.train, using the analytic gradient and a positive Hessian floor (e.g. 1e-3). Use the same 300 rounds, learning_rate 0.05, num_leaves 15 and colsample_bytree 0.3, and convert raw scores with a sigmoid in fit_predict. The idea is to put more gradient weight on molecules the boosted trees currently misclassify, which may help the ranking near the decision boundary. Leave the RandomForest member and the rank-average blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Focal-loss LightGBM via custom objective

backlog.spec: Before fitting the LightGBM member, create an augmented training set by adding a copy of the training rows generated by convex mixing: for each sampled pair (i, j) with lambda ~ Beta(0.4, 0.4) drawn from a seeded RNG, form x = lambda*x_i + (1-lambda)*x_j and y = lambda*y_i + (1-lambda)*y_j, then keep the soft label by fitting with LightGBM's cross-entropy objective ('cross_entropy' accepts labels in [0,1]). Mix only the quantile-clipped descriptor columns, and use the same Morgan bits from the nearer-to-lambda parent. Augment with about as many synthetic rows as there are real rows. Use the seed for all sampling. The RF member stays on the original data.
backlog.title: Mixup augmentation of descriptor rows for LightGBM

backlog.spec: Fit a quick 100-tree RandomForest on the training fold and compute each training molecule's out-of-bag probability of its own label. Rank the molecules by this difficulty score. Train the LightGBM member in staged fashion with lgb.train by setting per-row weights that start at 0 for the hardest 40% of molecules and are switched on linearly over the first 150 of 300 rounds (so the model first learns from the easy, consistent rows and then absorbs the hard ones). Implement the switch by rebuilding the Dataset with new weights at round 150, or by using a custom weight callback. Keep the RF member and the rank blend as they are.
backlog.title: Self-paced curriculum boosting

backlog.spec: Replace the single LightGBM member with LightGBM run in gradient-based one-side sampling mode (data_sample_strategy='goss' or boosting_type='goss', top_rate=0.2, other_rate=0.1), with a different random seed per bagged model. Train 5 such boosters on the full training fold with seeds derived from the seed argument, then average their rank-normalised predictions in place of the single LightGBM. The per-iteration gradient-based row sampling should reduce variance across fits without changing the descriptors or the RF member.
backlog.title: GOSS-style gradient-sampled boosting with row resampling

backlog.spec: Build a bagged ensemble of 15 small RandomForests (100 trees each, same max_features 0.3, n_jobs=-1). For each member draw a class-balanced subset: all positives plus an equal-size random sample of negatives, using a seeded RNG derived from the seed argument. Average the member probabilities and rank-normalise the result, then use it in place of the single RandomForest in the blend. The point is that each tree sees a balanced class prior, which may give rankings that differ from the full-data forest and add diversity to the rank average.
backlog.title: Balanced undersampling forest ensemble

backlog.spec: Before fitting the forest, split the standardized full-RDKit descriptor block into random feature subsets of size 8, and for each subset fit a PCA (sklearn, whitened=False) on a bootstrap sample of the training rows and store the rotation matrix. Build 25 trees with sklearn DecisionTreeClassifier (max_depth None, min_samples_leaf 1), where each tree sees the Morgan bits unchanged and the rotated descriptor components of all subsets. Average tree probabilities, rank-normalise, and add this rotation-forest score as a third rank-averaged member next to the existing blend. Store the rotation matrices and projection functions so the same transform is applied to test rows.
backlog.title: Rotation-forest style projected descriptor trees

backlog.spec: Standardise the clipped full-RDKit descriptor matrix on the training fold and reduce it to 20 principal components. Fit one multivariate Gaussian per class (mean and covariance with a ridge term 1e-2 added to the diagonal) on the training rows, and compute the test log-likelihood ratio log p(x|y=1) + log prior ratio. Convert that score to a probability with a sigmoid of its centred value, then rank-normalise it and add it as a third member with equal weight alongside the existing RF and LightGBM ranks. This is a deliberately different generative model that makes a Gaussian assumption about the descriptor distribution.
backlog.title: Generative Gaussian classifier on PCA-whitened descriptors

backlog.spec: Quantile-transform each clipped full-RDKit descriptor column using the training-fold quantiles (map to a uniform distribution, then to standard normal), and drop constant columns. For each test molecule find its k=15 nearest training molecules by Euclidean distance in this scaled descriptor space, weighting neighbours by 1/(distance+1e-3), and take the weighted positive fraction as the score. Rank-normalise the score and add it as a third equal-weight rank member. Unlike the Tanimoto fingerprint kNN already tried, this neighbourhood is defined by physicochemical properties, which the descriptor results suggest carry most of the signal.
backlog.title: Descriptor-space k-nearest-neighbour rank member

backlog.spec: Build a small interpretable rule model. Discretise each of the 11 physchem descriptors and the top 30 Morgan bits by frequency into quantile bins of 4 levels. Greedily grow a decision list of at most 12 rules: at each step pick the single (feature, threshold or bin, direction) whose covered training rows have the highest positive-rate lift with at least 20 covered molecules, add it to the list, remove the covered rows, and repeat. Score each test molecule by the Laplace-smoothed positive rate of the first rule it matches, with a fallback to the training base rate. Rank-normalise and add the result as an extra member of the rank average, using seed only to break ties.
backlog.title: Sparse greedy decision-list member

backlog.spec: Fit the existing RF+LightGBM rank blend on the training fold and obtain out-of-bag style predictions for the training molecules from a 5-fold inner split (same scaffold grouping not required). Mark training molecules whose inner prediction is confidently correct (probability above 0.8 for positives or below 0.2 for negatives) as easy. Refit the blend on the uncertain band only, meaning the molecules that are not easy, and use this second-stage model's rank scores for test molecules that fall in the uncertain band of the first-stage score (between its 25th and 75th percentile). For the other test molecules keep the first-stage rank score. Use the seed argument for all splits and keep the output in [0,1].
backlog.title: Two-stage confident-region cascade
